project.name: Skripsi_Bevan
project.description: Skripsi_Bevan is a Python research project that combines graph neural networks, diffusion models, and FAISS-based retrieval for weather nowcasting. It is built on PyTorch, PyTorch Geometric, and Open-Meteo data pipelines, with evaluation scripts and baseline MLP comparisons.

tour.title: Project Overview
tour.description: Start with the active documentation index, then explore the comprehensive knowledge base and research-methodology document. These files explain the project's goal: spatiotemporal precipitation nowcasting for the Gede-Pangrango region using ERA5 data, a canonical 5-node star graph, GNN encoding, retrieval augmentation, and diffusion generation.

tour.title: Training Pipeline Entry Point
tour.description: The training script is the main entry point that orchestrates the entire learning workflow. It ingests weather data, builds the star graph, precomputes retrieval contexts, trains the GNN and diffusion models, validates performance, and saves checkpoints.
tour.languageLesson: Python scripts often use an argparse helper to expose CLI hyperparameters and a single high-level function that wires data loaders, models, optimizers, and loggers together.

tour.title: Configuration & Graph Topology
tour.description: The central configuration module defines the canonical 5-node star topology and validates the feature schema before any model sees data. It also builds the star-shaped edge index and geospatial edge attributes that connect the main node to surrounding stations.
tour.languageLesson: Encapsulating topology helpers in a dedicated module makes the graph structure a first-class citizen: change the node list here and every downstream model, loader, and evaluation script updates consistently.

tour.title: Weather Data Ingestion
tour.description: The ingestion module downloads ERA5 reanalysis through Open-Meteo, validates that configured coordinates align with ERA5 grid cells, and persists tidy parquet files. This is the first stage of the pipeline that turns raw meteorology into machine-readable tabular data.

tour.title: Temporal Graph Data Loading
tour.description: The temporal loader converts tabular sequences into sliding-window PyTorch Geometric graph snapshots on the canonical 5-node star. It enforces the node-order contract, normalizes features and targets, and batches samples with a custom collate function.
tour.languageLesson: A PyTorch Dataset implements __getitem__ and __len__ so a DataLoader can batch samples; a custom collate function lets you stack irregular graph snapshots into a single mini-batch.

tour.title: Spatio-Temporal GNN Encoder
tour.description: The GNN model combines graph-attention spatial layers with causal temporal self-attention to encode each 5-node snapshot into a conditioned representation. This representation feeds the downstream diffusion forecaster and shapes how information propagates across stations and time.
tour.languageLesson: Message-passing neural networks alternate neighborhood aggregation (spatial reasoning) with sequence modeling (temporal reasoning) to capture both spatial correlations and temporal dynamics.

tour.title: Conditional Diffusion Forecaster
tour.description: The diffusion module implements a conditional DDPM/DDIM sampler that predicts precipitation and wet-event probabilities. The RainForecaster wraps the noise model into a high-level interface for generating ensemble nowcasts conditioned on GNN-encoded states.
tour.languageLesson: Diffusion models learn to reverse a gradual noising process, turning random noise into structured forecasts; conditioning on graph embeddings lets the model respect spatial and meteorological context.

tour.title: Retrieval-Augmented Context Store
tour.description: Historical weather context vectors are indexed in a FAISS-backed retrieval database. At inference time, the system queries nearest neighbors from the training set to enrich the diffusion condition with analogous past weather patterns.
tour.languageLesson: FAISS is a library for efficient approximate nearest-neighbor search over dense vectors, enabling memory-augmented models without storing the entire training set in GPU memory.

tour.title: Real-Time Inference Pipeline
tour.description: The inference module loads trained checkpoints and normalization statistics, builds the inference graphs, queries the retrieval store, runs diffusion sampling, and denormalizes outputs into physical units. It is the production path from raw conditions to nowcasts.
tour.languageLesson: Inference scripts usually separate model loading (heavy, done once) from the forward loop (repeated per sample) and handle device placement so the same code runs on CPU or CUDA.

tour.title: Evaluation Orchestration
tour.description: The final evaluation script benchmarks persistence, MLP, and diffusion-GNN scenarios, computes deterministic and probabilistic metrics, and produces comparison plots and reports. It is the main entry point for measuring model quality after training.
tour.languageLesson: A well-structured evaluation script seeds random state, loads the same test data for every scenario, and writes both machine-readable JSON metrics and human-readable plots for reproducible reporting.

tour.title: Probabilistic Metrics Library
tour.description: The metrics module collects verification scores such as RMSE, MAE, correlation, CRPS, Brier score, POD, FAR, CSI, and reliability diagrams. These metrics quantify both accuracy and forecast sharpness, which is essential for comparing ensemble and deterministic baselines.
tour.languageLesson: Continuous Ranked Probability Score (CRPS) generalizes MAE to probabilistic forecasts: a perfect deterministic forecast has CRPS equal to its MAE, while a sharp, well-calibrated ensemble can score lower.

tour.title: Baselines & Robustness Checks
tour.description: The MLP baseline and its training script provide a lightweight deterministic comparison, while the robustness evaluation script cross-checks forecasts across selected dry, median, and wet weekly windows. Together they show how the diffusion-GNN model performs under varying rainfall regimes.

tour.title: Tests & Model Contracts
tour.description: The test suite guards the canonical node ordering, temporal loader contracts, checkpoint metadata, and end-to-end inference smoke paths. These tests ensure that refactors do not silently break the 5-node star graph assumptions or the checkpoint format.
tour.languageLesson: Contract tests encode invariants that matter more than exact numerical outputs: if graph topology, node order, or checkpoint metadata changes, the test suite fails before bad predictions reach evaluation.

tour.title: Results & Reports
tour.description: Evaluation outputs include CSV timeseries, JSON metric summaries, and markdown reports for each scenario. The evaluation report summarizes deterministic and probabilistic metrics by variable, giving a concise view of which models excel at precipitation, wind, and humidity nowcasting.
tour.languageLesson: Splitting results into machine-readable JSON and human-readable markdown lets automated dashboards consume metrics while researchers can read the narrative report directly.
